title: What the AI Asset Management console inventories show: public AI apps, AI assets, AI resources, dashboard and usage insights

prose.text: Issues raised on these assets are in [[ai-security.asset-management.issues]], and the DLP engines behind the Data Security tab are in [[ai-security.asset-management.posture-policies]]. The hub is [[ai-security.asset-management]].

public-ai-time-ranges.statement: The Public AI Overview, Public AI Inventory - Gen AI, Endpoint AI and Embedded AI pages can each be filtered to Last 1 Day, Last 7 Days, Last 15 Days, Last Month or Last Quarter.

quotes: Filter the report for the Last 1 Day, Last 7 Days, Last 15 Days, Last Month, or Last Quarter.
Filter the report for the Last 1 Day, Last 7 Days, Last 15 Days, Last Month, or Last Quarter.
Filter the report for the Last 1 Day, Last 7 Days, Last 15 Days, Last Month, or Last Quarter.
Filter the report for the Last 1 Day, Last 7 Days, Last 15 Days, Last Month, or Last Quarter.

overview-widgets.statement: The Public AI Overview page (Public AI > Overview) shows Total Volume, Total Users, Upload Volume, Download Volume and Files Uploaded widgets for Gen AI apps, and a By Apps chart of the top 5 Gen AI apps with Allowed, Blocked or Isolated policy-action distribution.

quotes: Total Volume: View the total volume of Gen AI apps used in the organization.
Total Users: View the total number of users of Gen AI apps in your organization.
Upload Volume: View the total volume of data uploaded to Gen AI apps.
Download Volume: View the total volume of data downloaded from Gen AI apps.
Files Uploaded: View the total number of files uploaded to the AI apps.
By Apps: View the top 5 Gen AI apps used in the organization
View the top 5 Gen AI apps used in the organization with policy actions (Allowed, Blocked, or Isolated) distribution for each of the apps in the form of a bar chart.

overview-filters.statement: On the Public AI Overview page, the By Apps chart can be filtered to Gen AI or Embedded apps and by Total Bytes, Transactions or Users, and AI Usage by Locations by Transactions or Total Bytes.

quotes: By Apps: View the top 5 Gen AI apps used in the organization
You can filter data for the Gen AI or Embedded apps and by Total Bytes, Transactions, or Users.
AI Usage by Locations: View the AI apps usage by location in the form of a bar chart.
You can filter the data by total Transactions or Total Bytes.

gen-ai-risk-index.statement: On the Public AI Inventory - Gen AI page, the risk index rating scale runs from Very Low–1 to Very High–5, with Medium–3 in between.

quotes: The risk index rating is as follows:
- Very Low–1
- Medium–3
- Very High–5

gen-ai-users-locations.statement: In the Gen AI inventory list, Users counts unique authenticated users who accessed the application in the selected time range, and Locations counts unauthenticated locations from which it is accessed.

quotes: Users: The number of unique authenticated users who accessed the application within the specified time range.
Locations: The number of unauthenticated locations from where the application is accessed.

embedded-ai-volume.statement: On the Embedded AI inventory page, an app's Total Volume is the sum of upload and download bytes for both embedded and non-embedded AI traffic.

quotes: Total Volume: The sum of upload and download bytes of the application for both embedded and non-embedded AI traffic.

embedded-ai-definition.statement: Embedded AI apps are AI-powered features built directly into popular SaaS applications, as distinct from standalone generative AI tools.

quotes: Unlike standalone generative AI tools, Embedded AI apps are AI-powered features built directly into popular SaaS applications

risk-attributes-tab.statement: The detail page of a Gen AI app and of an Embedded AI app has a Risk Attributes tab with Hosting Information and Security Information; its listed risk attributes include a history of data breaches in the last three years.

quotes: Hosting Information: Details about where the AI application is hosted
history of data breaches in the last three years
Security Information: Security features and configurations of the AI application
Hosting Information: Details about where the AI application is hosted
history of data breaches in the last three years
Security Information: Security features and configurations of the AI application

endpoint-ai-top-apps.statement: The Endpoint AI inventory page shows the top 5 Endpoint AI apps by instances, and the count of detected application instances.

quotes: View the top 5 Endpoint AI apps by instances.
Instances: View the number of detected application instances.

endpoint-ai-versions.statement: The Versions table on an Endpoint AI app reports Code Signing Certificate Status as Valid Signature, Certificate Expired, Unsigned, Not Valid or Invalid Signature, and Threat Type as Benign, Malicious, Suspicious or Unknown, along with the MD5 hash.

quotes: i.e., Valid Signature, Certificate Expired, Unsigned, Not Valid, or Invalid Signature.
i.e., Benign, Malicious, Suspicious, or Unknown.
MD5: The MD5 hash of the application.
Code Signing Certificate Status: The code signing status of the application
Threat Type: The threat type of the application

identities-scope.statement: AI Security detects identities in onboarded AWS, Azure and GCP cloud accounts, including managed and unmanaged databases, and Snowflake; an identity is a user, device, application or service that can access data stores containing sensitive data.

quotes: An identity represents a user, device, application, or service that can access data stores containing sensitive data in the cloud environment.
AI Security detects identities in all the onboarded cloud accounts (AWS, Azure, and GCP), including managed and unmanaged databases, and Snowflake.

identities-fields.statement: The Identities article places the page at AI Infrastructure > Identities and says it shows an Access Type (with Read, Edit or Full Access as examples) and a Risk Posture (with Dormant Identity and MFA Disabled as examples) for each identity.

quotes: On the Identities page (AI Infrastructure > Identities), you can do the following:
Access Type: The permission level granted to the entity for the selected resource, e.g., Read, Edit, or Full Access.
Risk Posture: The security posture assigned to the identity (Dormant Identity, MFA Disabled, etc.).

models-subtypes.statement: The Models by Subtype widget classifies model origin as Foundation (vendor-provided pre-trained base model used as-is), Free-Tuning (foundation model trained further on the organization's data), Imported, Unknown or Others.

quotes: Foundation: A vendor-provided, pre-trained base model, e.g., an LLM or embedding model and used as-is.
Free-Tuning: A foundation model trained further on your organization’s data for specific tasks.
Imported: A model introduced from an external source
Unknown: The subtype could not be determined from the available metadata.
Others: Models that do not match the listed subtypes.

models-type-filter.statement: The Type filter on the AI Assets - Models page supports Managed (managed by a cloud service provider), Unmanaged (deployed and managed independently), Custom (built and trained in-house) and Registry Model (from a model registry or public repository).

quotes: Managed: AI models that are fully managed by a cloud service provider (CSP)
Unmanaged: AI models that are deployed and managed independently, outside a CSP's managed offering.
Custom: AI models that are built and trained in-house by the organization.
Registry Model: AI models that are sourced from a model registry or public repository

models-risk-meaning.statement: The Models by Risk widget rates a model's vulnerability to adversarial exploits (prompt injection, jailbreaking, unauthorized data extraction) as Critical, High, Medium or Low, and measures attack resistance rather than the severity of known open issues.

quotes: Models by Risk: View distribution of the model's vulnerability to adversarial exploits, such as prompt injection, jailbreaking, and unauthorized data extraction.
Ratings are categorized as Critical, High, Medium, or Low.
This score specifically measures the model's attack resistance rather than the severity of known open issues.

models-model-security-tab.statement: A benchmark-based model risk score is shown only when a benchmark has been run; the Model Security tab is visible if the model type is unmanaged and the risk score is greater than 0, and is described as only for unmanaged models.

quotes: Benchmark-based risk score is shown only when a benchmark has been run.
If the model type is unmanaged and if the risk score is greater than 0, another tab, Model Security, is visible.
Model Security (Only for unmanaged models)

models-benchmark-dimensions.statement: The Model Security Performance Summary reports benchmark results across four quality dimensions (Security, Safety, Hallucinations, Business Alignment), with No System Prompt, Basic System Prompt and Hardened System Prompt tabs.

quotes: Performance Summary: Indicates the benchmark results across four quality dimensions, i.e., Security, Safety, Hallucinations, and Business Alignment.
No System Prompt
Basic System Prompt
Hardened System Prompt

models-supply-chain.statement: For an unmanaged model, Model Supply Chain Risk gives a composite Risk Score on a scale of 0 to 100 and a Critical/High/Medium/Low severity rolled up from it; the Files check uses security scan results from Hugging Face and labels suspicious files Unsafe, Caution or Suspicious.

quotes: Risk Score: Indicates the composite supply chain risk for this model on a scale of 0 to 100.
Severity: Indicates the severity category, i.e., Critical, High, Medium, or Low derived by rolling up the underlying numeric risk score.
security scan results (scanned by Hugging Face)
Unsafe, Caution, and Suspicious labels are assigned to suspicious files.

models-usage-tabs.statement: The Usage and Top 10 Users tabs on a model's detail page are available only for AWS managed and custom models.

quotes: Usage (Only for AWS managed and custom models)
Top 10 Users (Only for AWS managed and custom models)

models-mcp-export.statement: The AI Assets - Models and AI Assets - MCP Servers pages export their data as an Excel file with the Export button.

quotes: Click Export to export the data and download the report as an Excel file.
Click Export to export the data and download the report as an Excel file.

mcp-risk-level.statement: An MCP server's Risk Level indicates its potential blast radius if compromised, based on command execution, file write or delete, credential access and outbound network calls; Critical means it can do all of these and Low means primarily read-only with no system-level access.

quotes: Indicates the potential blast radius if this MCP server is compromised.
The rating is based on capabilities such as system command execution, file write or delete access, credential storage or access, and outbound (external) network calls.
Critical means the server can execute commands, modify files, handle credentials, and contact external services.
Low means the server is primarily read-only, with no system-level access.

mcp-tool-fields.statement: The Tools tab of an MCP server shows, per tool, whether it has File Access, Network Access, Code Execution and Process Access, plus the File Path it can access or targets.

quotes: File Access: Indicates whether the tool has file access or not.
Network Access: Indicates whether the tool has network access or not.
Code Execution: Indicates whether the tool can execute code or system commands
Process Access: Indicates if the tool can view, start, stop, signal, or attach to running processes
File Path: The file-system path(s) the tool can access or that the tool targets

mcp-filters.statement: The MCP Servers page Type filter returns servers by whether they are remote or local, and the Asset Risk filter risk signals include execution capabilities, file deletion operations, directory traversal, external network access, credential storage/handling and processing of sensitive data.

quotes: Type: Returns MCP servers based on whether they are remote or local.
Execution capabilities
File deletion operations
Directory traversal
External network access
Credential storage/handling
Processing of sensitive data (for example, PII)

agents-definition.statement: In Zscaler AI Security, agents are AI orchestration workflows or chatbots that connect LLMs, enterprise data sources and tools (including other agents), and are treated as first-class AI assets.

quotes: agents are AI orchestration workflows or chatbots that can connect LLMs, enterprise data sources (knowledge), and tools, including agents to complete tasks or workflows.
they are treated as first-class AI assets

agents-risk-widgets.statement: The Agents page describes an agent's overall risk level as rolled up from its most severe issues (its Risk Level field text elsewhere on the page differs, see the page-copy-errors gap); the Agents by Risk widget uses Critical, High, Medium, Low or Unknown, and another widget counts agents with access to sensitive data and publicly exposed agents.

quotes: overall risk level, rolled up from its most severe issues
Agents by Risk: View the distribution of agents by severity of risk, categorized as Critical, High, Medium, Low, or Unknown.
View the number of agents that can access sensitive data and view the number of agents that are publicly exposed.

data-security-tab.statement: On the agent detail page the Data Security tab is visible if data is filtered by sensitive data; for agents and for data stores it lists Matched Files, Triggers, DLP Engines, DLP Dictionaries, Document Categories and Document Types.

quotes: Data Security (visible if data is filtered by sensitive data)
Matched Files: The number of files that matched the DLP engines.
Triggers: Number of alerts raised for the resource.
DLP Engines: The DLP engines that match sensitive records.
DLP Dictionaries: The dictionaries associated with the DLP engines.
Document Categories: The category of document detected in the resource.
Document Types: The number of documents detected in the resource.
Matched Files: The number of files that matched the DLP engines.
Triggers: Number of alerts raised for the resource.
DLP Engines: The DLP engines that match sensitive records.
DLP Dictionaries: The dictionaries associated with the DLP engines.
Document Categories: The category of document detected in the resource.
Document Types: The number of documents detected in the resource.

libraries-status-default.statement: On the AI Software Libraries page a library's Status default value is Pending Review, and the Actions icon lets an admin mark a library Sanctioned or Unsanctioned to approve or reject its use.

quotes: Status: The approval status of the library. The default value is Pending Review.
Actions: Click the Action icon and select Sanctioned or Unsanctioned to approve or reject the package's use in the organization.

libraries-risk-bands.statement: The Supply Chain Risk tab of an AI software library maps the overall risk score to Low 0–33, Medium 34–55, High 55–74 and Critical 75–100 (as printed; Medium and High both include 55).

quotes: Medium: 34–55
High: 55–74
Critical: 75–100

libraries-categories.statement: A library's Total Categories is always five (Security, Dependencies, Quality, Maintenance, Compliance), and Total Issues is the number of failed checks across all categories, each failed check being one issue.

quotes: Total Categories: The number of risk categories evaluated for this package.
This score is always five and includes, Security, Dependencies, Quality, Maintenance, and Compliance.
Total Issues: Total number of failed checks across all categories. Each failed check is one issue.

libraries-tab-visibility.statement: The Supply Chain Risk tab on an AI software library is visible only when a Supply Chain Risk Score is available; otherwise the tab is hidden.

quotes: This tab is enabled and visible only when a Supply Chain Risk Score is available for the model. If the score is not available, the tab remains hidden.

libraries-license-types.statement: The AI Software Libraries by License Type widget groups licenses into Permissive and Copyleft; the Permissive example list includes AGPL-3.0 and the Copyleft example list includes AGPL.

quotes: Permissive Licenses: Have fewer redistribution requirements, e.g., AGPL-3.0, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, and MIT.
Copyleft Licenses: Require derivative works to be open-sourced and may increase compliance risk in commercial deployments, e.g., GPL and AGPL.

data-stores-widgets.statement: On the Data Stores page, Data Stores by Risk Level reflects the severity of a data store's open security issues (None meaning no open issues), and Sensitive Data Exposed to AI counts data stores holding sensitive data (PII, PHI, PCI) connected to at least one AI model, agent or workload.

quotes: Data Stores by Risk Level: Distribution of data stores by severity level among the data store’s open security issues.
If the value is None, no open issues are currently detected.
Sensitive Data Exposed to AI: Distribution of data stores that contain sensitive data, such as PII, PHI, PCI, and are connected to at least one AI model, agent, or workload.

data-stores-graph.statement: The graph for an AI service on the Data Stores page depicts its access path (Azure AI Foundry Hub or AWS Bedrock Knowledge Base) to the storage account containing sensitive data, and AI Security also detects whether the AI service is publicly exposed to the internet.

quotes: It depicts the access path for the AI service (Azure AI Foundry Hub or AWS Bedrock Knowledge Base) where it has access to the storage account containing sensitive data.
AI Security also detects if the AI service is publicly exposed to the internet

dashboard-asset-explorer.statement: The AI Security Dashboard's AI Infrastructure tab has an Asset Explorer with AI Assets (models, MCP servers, agents, apps), AI Resources (data stores, AI software libraries, AI guardrails, identities, workloads) and Data Classification for AI tabs.

quotes: Use this tab to view AI-related infrastructure connected to your organization
The Asset Explorer section displays a visual summary of your AI Inventory across connected cloud accounts and repositories.
AI Assets: Use this tab to view an inventory of AI asset entities—models, MCP servers, agents, and apps
AI Resources: Use this tab to view an inventory of entities involved in AI resource usage, such as data stores, AI software libraries, AI guardrails, identities, and workloads.
Data Classification for AI: Use this tab to view an inventory of entities involved in AI data classification categories, such as Source Code, Legal, and Technical.

dashboard-red-teaming.statement: The Dashboard's Red Teaming tab shows red-teamed AI assets by Health Score (critical, low, medium, high or unknown) and by Availability (internal or customer-facing), and lists onboarded assets not yet red teamed, whose security posture is unknown.

quotes: Health Score: Displays a segmented view of a health score categorized as critical, low, medium, high, or unknown.
Availability: Displays a segmented view based on whether the asset is internal or customer-facing.
View a list of AI assets that have been onboarded but have not yet been red teamed. Since no test runs have been executed, their security posture is unknown.

usage-insights-tabs.statement: The Usage Insights page (Public AI > Usage Insights) has Users, Departments, Locations and Sensitive Data tabs.

quotes: Use this tab to view usage insights for users.
Use this tab to view usage insights for departments.
Use this tab to view usage insights for locations.
Use this tab to view usage insights for sensitive data.

usage-insights-filters.statement: On Usage Insights, the Sensitive Data tab filters by Content Type (DLP Engine, DLP Dictionary or ML Category) and the Departments and Locations tabs filter by Application Type (Gen AI or Embedded AI) and policy actions Allowed, Blocked or Isolated.

quotes: Filter the data for specific Policy Actions taken (Allowed, Blocked, or Isolated) or Content Type (DLP Engine, DLP Dictionary, or ML Category).
Filter the data for specific Departments, Application Type (Gen AI or Embedded AI), or Policy Actions taken (Allowed, Blocked, or Isolated).
Filter the data for specific Locations, Application Type (Gen AI or Embedded AI), or Policy Actions taken (Allowed, Blocked, or Isolated).

identities-path.summary: The Identities article prints the page path as AI Infrastructure > Identities, while the 2026 release notes print AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Identities.

positions.says: The Identities page is at AI Infrastructure > Identities.

quotes: On the Identities page (AI Infrastructure > Identities), you can do the following:

positions.says: The Identities page is at AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Identities.

quotes: how identities are represented, visualized, and categorized on the AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Identities page.

identities-path.impact: The captured pages do not settle which path the console shows; navigate by what the console displays.

time-range-semantics.title: Whether Public AI Last Month and Last Quarter are calendar or rolling periods
time-range-semantics.detail: The pages list Last 1 Day, Last 7 Days, Last 15 Days, Last Month and Last Quarter but do not say whether the last two are calendar or rolling windows.

risk-score-bands.title: Risk score bands for MCP servers and agents
risk-score-bands.detail: The captured pages give score bands for AI software libraries and model scan findings only; the Risk Score bands for MCP servers and agents are not stated.

page-copy-errors.title: Which field descriptions on the Agents, Data Stores and Identities pages are copy errors
page-copy-errors.detail: The Agents page repeats server wording for Type (Remote or Local) and identity wording for Asset Risk; the Data Stores page repeats the identity wording for Asset Risk and describes Lifecycle as stages of an AI agent; Agents and Data Stores describe Cloud Account as the account in which the model is located; the Agents and Data Stores Risk Level field copies the MCP blast-radius wording (capabilities such as command execution and file write or delete), which conflicts with the agent risk roll-up and the data store open-issue severity widgets; the Models page's Model Risk filter text (known vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, non-compliance) conflicts with the Models by Risk widget text (attack resistance, not open issues); the Models page labels the subtype Free-Tuning in one place and Fine-tuning in another; the Identities by Status widget is described as a distribution of software libraries by governance status. No claim is written from these descriptions.

governance-status-labels.title: Which governance status names MCP servers and libraries use
governance-status-labels.detail: The MCP Servers page names the governance status Approved, Disapproved or Pending Review in one place, Sanctioned, Unsanctioned or Pending in the widget, and Pending, Sanctioned or Unsanctioned in the Status field. The AI Software Libraries page lists Unreviewed (awaiting review) in one place and a Pending Review default in another. The pages do not say which labels the console shows.

view-permissions.title: Which roles can view the inventories
view-permissions.detail: The pages do not say which administrator roles or permissions are needed to view the AI Asset Management inventories.

navigation-paths.title: Which navigation path each page uses
navigation-paths.detail: The pages name different paths for the same product area (the Identities page is AI Infrastructure > Identities in its article and AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Identities in release notes, recorded as a divergence); no path is recorded as a fact beyond what the claims quote.
